rows.question: How do I change the address on my driving licence?
keyFacts: It does not cost anything to change your address with DVLA
You can apply online (or by post)

answer.answer: Update your address online at GOV.UK (search 'change address driving licence'). It's free. You'll need your driving licence number and your National Insurance number. Tell DVLA as soon as your address changes, because failing to update your details can lead to a fine of up to £1,000. You can keep driving while you wait for any updated licence.

rows.question: How much does it cost to renew my driving licence when I turn 70?
keyFacts: Renewing your driving licence at 70 or over is free

answer.answer: It's free. When you reach 70 you must renew your photocard licence, and after that you renew every 3 years, always at no cost. Be wary of third-party sites that charge a fee for this.

keyFacts: You must be at least 15 years and 9 months old

keyFacts: A replacement licence costs £20 online

You can also apply for a free replacement if your licence was stolen and you have a crime reference number, but the standard fee applies otherwise. Check the GOV.UK page for the current fee before applying.

rows.question: How long do penalty points stay on my licence?
keyFacts: Penalty points/endorsements stay on your driving record for 4 or 11 years, depending on the offence

answer.answer: Most penalty points stay on your licence for 4 years from the date of the offence. Some offences, such as drink or drug driving, stay for 11 years.

rows.question: How much does the car theory test cost?

rows.question: How do I tell DVLA my car is off the road?
keyFacts: Tell DVLA online (or by phone/post) that the vehicle is off the road: a SORN
You get a refund for any full months of remaining tax

answer.answer: Make a Statutory Off-Road Notification (SORN) online at GOV.UK. It's free and takes a few minutes. You'll need your vehicle's registration number and details from your V5C logbook. Once the SORN is accepted, the vehicle can't be driven or kept on a public road until it's taxed again, though it can stay on private land. If you had tax left when you made the SORN, you can get a refund for the full untaxed months.

rows.question: Can I get a refund on my vehicle tax if I sell my car?
keyFacts: You cancel vehicle tax by telling DVLA you no longer have the vehicle (for example sold, scrapped or off the road); there is no other way
You get a refund for any full months of remaining tax

answer.answer: Yes. If you sell or transfer the vehicle, you can get a refund for each complete month of vehicle tax left, if you apply for it. The refund does not include any part-month. You can apply online on GOV.UK or by post, and you need the vehicle's registration number and the V5C (logbook) details. The buyer must tax the car before they drive it on the road.

Vehicles used by a disabled person can be exempt

Exemptions must be claimed or declared through DVLA, and the vehicle must still be taxed or SORN as appropriate.

keyFacts: The minimum penalty is a £100 fine and 3 penalty points
You could be disqualified if you reach 12 or more points within 3 years

answer.answer: For most speeding offences in England, Scotland and Wales, the standard fixed penalty is a £100 fine and 3 penalty points on your licence. Some drivers are offered a speed awareness course instead, which avoids points. If the case goes to court, the fine can be higher and you can get more points or a driving ban. Accumulating 12 or more points within 3 years usually means a minimum 6-month ban. Drivers within 2 years of passing their test who reach 6 points lose their licence and must reapply.

rows.question: Can I drive if I have diabetes?
keyFacts: You must tell DVLA if your insulin treatment lasts (or will last) over 3 months
You do not need to tell DVLA if the diabetes is treated by diet alone

answer.answer: Yes, in most cases you can drive with diabetes, but you must tell the DVLA if you take insulin or medication that can cause hypos (such as sulfonylureas or glinides). You don't need to tell them if you control diabetes with diet alone or with medicines that don't cause hypos. Before driving, check your blood glucose and carry hypo treatment. On long journeys, test about every 2 hours. Don't drive if your blood sugar is low or you feel a hypo coming on. After a hypo, wait at least 45 minutes after recovering before driving. Lorry and bus licences (Group 2) have stricter rules, and insulin use there is generally restricted.

rows.question: What are the eyesight rules for driving?
keyFacts: You must be able to read a number plate from 20 metres away
Minimum visual acuity of decimal 0.5 (6/12) on the Snellen scale, with glasses or contact lenses if needed

answer.answer: You must be able to read a car number plate from 20 metres away, using glasses or contact lenses if you need them. You must also tell the DVLA if you have an eye condition or any vision problem that could affect your driving, or if you have sight in only one eye. Other requirements include an adequate field of vision, and you must not drive if your eyesight is below the legal standard.

rows.question: How do I change the photo on my driving licence?
keyFacts: It costs £14 to change the photo online
You do this by renewing your licence (online, or by post for £17)

answer.answer: Apply for a replacement photocard licence on GOV.UK (usually £20 for a GB licence). You'll need a recent digital photo that meets the rules: taken within the last month, plain light background, face clearly visible and centred, no sunglasses or head covering unless for religious or medical reasons. You can usually upload it during the online application. If you can't upload one, you'll be told how to send a printed photo instead. Your old licence stays valid until the new one arrives, but you should still tell DVLA about any significant change in appearance. Check the current fee and photo requirements on GOV.UK before applying.

rows.question: What do the codes on my driving licence mean?
keyFacts: The codes on the back of the licence set conditions you must meet to drive
Examples: 01 eyesight correction (glasses or contact lenses); 78 automatic transmission only

answer.answer: Your licence has two kinds of codes. (1) Entitlement categories in section 12 show which vehicles you can drive, such as B (car up to 3,500kg and 8 passenger seats), A (motorcycle), C (lorry) and D (bus). (2) Restriction and endorsement codes in section 10 show conditions or limits, such as 01 (must wear glasses or contact lenses) or 78 (automatic vehicles only). Check the restriction codes against the official DVLA list, since codes vary and it is the full list that applies to you.

rows.question: How do I swap my paper driving licence for a photocard?
keyFacts: You do not need to exchange a valid paper licence unless you change your address or name, want to do Driver CPC training, or it is damaged, lost or stolen
It is free if you changed your name or address and still have the paper licence
Otherwise a new photocard licence costs £20

answer.answer: Apply online at GOV.UK for a photocard licence (you'll need a valid passport or other accepted ID, a UK passport-style photo, and your National Insurance number if you have one). You can also apply by post using the paper form. The photocard is sent to your address, and your paper licence stops being valid once the new one is issued, so keep it until then. Check the fee on GOV.UK when you apply, as it can change. Northern Ireland licences are handled by the DVA rather than GOV.UK.

rows.question: How much does the driving test cost?
keyFacts: The car driving test costs £62 on weekdays
It costs £75 on evenings, weekends and bank holidays

answer.answer: The car practical driving test costs £62 on weekdays and £75 on evenings, weekends and bank holidays. The car theory test costs £23. Fees can change, so check GOV.UK before booking.

rows.question: How do I change my driving test appointment?
keyFacts: You can change a car driving test only 2 times
You must change it yourself; your instructor is not allowed to

answer.answer: Sign in to your DVSA booking account on GOV.UK and choose to change or cancel the test. You can change or cancel for free up to 3 clear working days before the test; if you do it later than that, you may lose the booking fee. If you can't use the online service, call the DVSA practical driving test booking line.

rows.question: How do I tax a car if I haven't received a tax reminder?
keyFacts: You can tax online with the 11-digit reference number from your V5C (or the 12-digit number on the green new keeper slip)
You can also tax by phone or at a Post Office

answer.answer: You don't need a reminder to tax your vehicle. Go to gov.uk/vehicle-tax, enter the vehicle registration number, and pay by card. The car must have a valid MOT (if it's 3 years old or more) and valid insurance before you can tax it. If the car is off the road and not being used, make a SORN declaration instead. Driving or parking on a public road while untaxed can lead to a fine, so tax the vehicle as soon as you can.

rows.question: I've just bought a used car. What do I need to do to tax it and get it registered in my name?

The seller usually registers a used vehicle for you, online or by post

They should complete their section (the 'Seller' part, including the date of sale) and you complete the 'New keeper' section, then send it to DVLA (or use the online service at gov.uk to tell DVLA you've bought it). You must tell DVLA within 30 days of buying, and a new V5C will be posted to you in your name. 2) Tax it at gov.uk/vehicle-tax before driving it on public roads. You'll need the registration number, and the car must have valid insurance and, if it's over 3 years old, a valid MOT (unless you're driving it to a pre-booked MOT). Vehicle Excise Duty is charged from the date you tax it, at the rate for the car's CO2 emissions and fuel type. 3) Make sure you have insurance in your name before driving it.

rows.question: My car has been written off. What do I tell DVLA and what happens to my vehicle tax?
keyFacts: You must tell DVLA the vehicle was written off and scrapped by your insurer
You get a vehicle tax refund for any full months left

answer.answer: If the car is being scrapped or taken off the road, tell DVLA using the online 'Tell DVLA vehicle is off the road' (SORN) service, or send the V5C (registration certificate) to DVLA. If it goes to an Authorised Treatment Facility, the facility normally notifies DVLA for you, but check you have the V5C sent off. You can claim a refund for each full calendar month of vehicle tax left, which you can do online at gov.uk/vehicle-tax-refund. If you keep the car and it's not being used on the road, you must declare it SORN; if you keep it and drive it, you must keep it taxed. Your insurer records the write-off category (Cat A, B, S, etc.) on the salvage and insurance databases, so you don't need to report the category to DVLA. Your insurer can confirm the salvage category if you're unsure.

rows.question: I'm over 70 and have a medical condition. How do I renew my driving licence?
keyFacts: You can renew online for free from 70 if you meet the eyesight requirement and nothing prevents you from driving
You must tell DVLA about medical conditions that affect your driving

answer.answer: From age 70 your photocard licence must be renewed every 3 years. DVLA will send a reminder (form D46P) before it expires, or you can renew online at GOV.UK. Renewal is free. You must also tell DVLA about any medical condition that could affect your driving, even if you don't think it's serious. Since you have a condition, DVLA will likely send form D1 (a medical questionnaire) with your renewal, and it may ask your GP or consultant for more information. Keep driving only while you're fit to do so. Failing to declare a condition can lead to a fine of up to £1,000 and invalidated insurance. If you're unsure what to declare, contact DVLA on 0300 790 6806 or check GOV.UK's medical conditions guidance.

rows.question: Will my appeal against a speeding fine succeed?

answer.answer: I can't predict whether your appeal will succeed, as that depends on your evidence and the grounds you raise. Successful challenges usually rely on a specific defence, such as: you weren't the driver and can show who was; the notice was not served or sent within the required time limit; the notice or procedure had errors; the camera or speed-measuring equipment was not working or not properly calibrated, or the camera was not set up as required; or there were exceptional circumstances (a legal defence like necessity, which is rarely accepted for speeding). Check the deadline on your notice and whether it is a Fixed Penalty Notice or a court summons, as the options and time limits differ. A magistrates' court decides contested cases.

rows.question: How much income tax will I pay on a company car?

answer.answer: You don't pay tax on the car itself. It's a benefit-in-kind, so the taxable amount is the car's list price (including extras, with a cap) multiplied by a percentage set by its CO2 emissions or electric range. That taxable amount is added to your salary and taxed at your income tax rate (20%, 40% or 45% in England, Wales and Northern Ireland; Scotland has its own bands). For example, an electric car at 3% (the 2025/26 rate) on a £40,000 list price gives a £1,200 taxable benefit, so a basic-rate taxpayer pays about £240 a year. Petrol and diesel cars have higher percentages. Check your exact percentage and any employer-paid fuel charge on GOV.UK.

rows.question: How do I set up a Direct Debit to pay my vehicle tax?

answer.answer: Set up Direct Debit when you tax the vehicle online at GOV.UK. Choose the option to pay by Direct Debit, then enter your vehicle registration number and bank details (sort code and account number). You'll need a UK bank account. Direct Debit is set up on the vehicle tax service, not through your bank. Check the GOV.UK vehicle tax page for current options, such as monthly payments and whether you can add Direct Debit to a vehicle that is already taxed.
